script: The first time Hitler tried to steal a country, the plan collapsed in a single afternoon. On July 25, 1934, more than a hundred and fifty SS men dressed as Austrian police stormed the chancellery in Vienna. A leaked warning had emptied the building minutes earlier, but Chancellor Dollfuss stayed at his post. They shot him in the throat and left him bleeding on a sofa, refusing him a doctor. Across the city, other Nazis seized the radio station and announced to the whole country a new government that did not exist. But here is the twist nobody expects, the man who stopped Hitler that day was Mussolini. The Italian dictator rushed four divisions to the mountain border and made it clear he would go to war for Austria. Hitler backed down within hours, denied everything, and abandoned his own men to the gallows. Thirteen of the plotters were hanged, and Hitler pretended he had never heard their names. Dollfuss never got his doctor, and the country Hitler failed to steal that afternoon finally fell to him four years later, without a single shot.
